    if binding not in BINDING_NAMES:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown binding: {binding!r}")
    issues = _errors(input_doc, "execution-input")
    if issues:
        raise PortError("INPUT_INVALID", "execution-input does not match exec/v1", {"issues": issues})
    issues = _errors(policy, "run-policy")
    if issues:
        raise PortError("POLICY_INVALID", "run-policy does not match exec/v1", {"issues": issues})
    for role_id, manifest in roles.items():
        issues = _errors(manifest, "role-manifest")
        if issues:
            raise PortError("INPUT_INVALID", f"role manifest {role_id!r} does not match exec/v1", {"issues": issues})
    current = settings if settings is not None else orch_settings.defaults()
    created = now or datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
    refuse_stale = current.capabilities_stale == "refuse"
    minimum = input_doc["route"]["minimum"]
    ordered = _order(policy["stages"])
    primary = next((stage for stage in ordered if stage["kind"] == "primary"), None)
    primary_provider = (primary.get("provider") or provider) if primary else None
    stages, refusals, decisions, blocked = [], [], [], []
    proof, warnings = {}, {}
    for stage in ordered:
        if stage["kind"] not in MODEL_KINDS:
            continue
        manifest = roles.get(ROLE_ALIASES.get(stage["role"], stage["role"]))
        if manifest is None:
            raise PortError("ROLE_UNKNOWN", f"stage {stage['id']!r} uses role {stage['role']!r} without a manifest")
        model_class = stage.get("model_class") or manifest["model_class_min"]
        if stage["kind"] == "primary" and CLASS_RANK[model_class] < CLASS_RANK[minimum["class"]]:
            raise PortError("ROUTE_UNDERSHOOT", f"stage {stage['id']!r} class {model_class!r} is below the "
                            f"input minimum {minimum['class']!r}")
        effort = stage.get("effort") or minimum["effort"]
        stage_provider = stage.get("provider") or provider
        if not stage_provider:
            raise PortError("INPUT_INVALID", f"stage {stage['id']!r} has no provider; pass one")
        cap = capabilities.get((binding, stage_provider))
        stale = cap is not None and is_stale(cap, created)
        if cap is not None:
            proof[stage_provider] = _proof_entry(binding, stage_provider, cap, stale)
        base = {"stage_id": stage["id"], "role": stage["role"], "kind": stage["kind"], "provider": stage_provider}
        reason_codes = []
        try:
            _stage_requirements(binding, policy, stage, manifest, cap, stage_provider, primary_provider,
                                refuse_stale=refuse_stale, now=created)
            if stale:  # only reached when stale records are warned about
                reason_codes.append("CAPABILITY_STALE")
                warnings[stage_provider] = {"code": "CAPABILITY_STALE", "message":
                                            f"the capability record for ({binding}, {stage_provider}) was fresh until "
                                            f"{cap['fresh_until']}"}
            resolved = {"class": model_class}
            if cap["model"]["set"] != "unsupported":
                resolved["model"] = _catalog(lambda: catalog.resolve_model(stage_provider, model_class), "model.set")
                base["model"] = resolved["model"]
            if cap["effort"]["set"] != "unsupported":
                resolved["effort"] = _catalog(lambda: catalog.resolve_effort(stage_provider, effort), "effort.set")
                base["effort"] = effort
            base["capability_ref"] = cap["_path"]
            base["delivery"] = {"mode": cap["skill_delivery"]["mode"], "paths": []}
            delivered = (skills or {}).get(manifest["role_id"]) or (skills or {}).get(stage["role"])
            if delivered:
                base["delivery"]["skills"] = [dict(item) for item in delivered]
            extra = project(input_doc, base, manifest, cap, resolved) if project else {}
        except Unmet as unmet:
            refusals.append({"stage_id": stage["id"], "capability": unmet.capability, "reason": unmet.reason,
                             "reason_code": unmet.code, "chain": _chain(unmet, cap)})
            decisions.append({"stage_id": stage["id"], "kind": "route", "chosen": "none", "tie_break": "policy-order",
                              "considered": [{"candidate": stage_provider, "accepted": False,
                                              "reason_codes": [unmet.code]}]})
            if stage["required"]:
                blocked.append(unmet.code)
            continue
        chosen = f"{stage_provider}/{resolved.get('model', model_class)}"
        decisions.append({"stage_id": stage["id"], "kind": "route", "chosen": chosen, "tie_break": "policy-order",
                          "considered": [{"candidate": stage_provider, "accepted": True,
                                          "reason_codes": reason_codes}]})
        stages.append({**base, **extra})
    decisions.append(engine_decision if engine_decision is not None else
                     {"stage_id": "*", "kind": "binding", "chosen": binding,
                      "considered": [{"candidate": binding, "accepted": True, "reason_codes": ["ENGINE_FROM_FLAG"]}]})
    config = {"digest": orch_settings.digest(current), "values": orch_settings.affecting(current)}
    digests = _digests(input_doc, policy, roles, binding, capabilities, catalog, config["digest"],
                       model_catalog_doc, launch_catalog_doc)
    plan = {
        "$schema": contracts.URN_PREFIX + "launch-plan:v1",
        "contract_version": CONTRACT_VERSION,
        "binding": binding,
        "run_id": "dry-" + input_doc["digest"][:12],
        "input_digest": input_doc["digest"],
        "policy_id": policy["policy_id"],
        "dry_run": True,
        "stages": stages,
        "refusals": refusals,
        "created_at": created,
        "digests": digests,
        "config": config,
        "modules": [{"id": "aicore", "version": aicore.__version__}, {"id": "orch", "version": orch.__version__}],
        "decisions": decisions,
        "policy_decision": {"decision": "refuse" if blocked else "allow",
                            "reason_codes": list(dict.fromkeys(blocked)), "policy_digest": digests["policy"]},
        "proof": {"capabilities": [proof[name] for name in sorted(proof)],
                  "warnings": [warnings[name] for name in sorted(warnings)]},
    }
    if submission_id is not None:
        plan["submission_id"] = submission_id
    plan["digest"] = contracts.canonical_digest(plan)
    issues = _errors(plan, "launch-plan")
    if issues:
        raise PortError("INPUT_INVALID", "prepared launch-plan does not match exec/v1", {"issues": issues})
    if blocked:
        raise PortError("CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED", "a required stage needs a capability the binding lacks",
                        {"launch_plan": plan})
    return plan


def _catalog(lookup: Callable[[], str], capability: str) -> str:
    try:
        return lookup()
    except CatalogError as error:
        raise Unmet(capability, str(error), "CATALOG_UNKNOWN") from error


class Binding:
    """Shared parts of a binding. A subclass sets ``binding`` and implements ``project``."""

    binding = ""

    def __init__(self, out: str | Path, *, catalog: Catalog, roles_dir: str | Path | None = None,
                 capabilities: Mapping[tuple[str, str], dict] | None = None, cwd: str = ".",
                 now: str | None = None, settings: orch_settings.Settings | None = None,
                 submission_id: str | None = None, skills: Mapping[str, list] | None = None,
                 engine_decision: dict | None = None):
        self.out = Path(out)
        self.catalog = catalog
        self.roles_dir = roles_dir
        self._capabilities = capabilities if capabilities is not None else load_capabilities()
        self.cwd = cwd
        self.now = now
        self.settings = settings
        self.submission_id = submission_id
        self.skills = skills
        self.engine_decision = engine_decision
        self._files: list[tuple[Path, str]] = []

    def capabilities(self) -> list[dict]:
        return [{key: value for key, value in record.items() if key != "_path"}
                for (binding, _), record in sorted(self._capabilities.items()) if binding == self.binding]

    def prepare(self, input_doc: dict, policy: dict, roles: Mapping[str, dict], *,
                provider: str | None = None, dry_run: bool = True) -> dict:
        if not dry_run:
            raise PortError("NOT_IMPLEMENTED", "prepare without dry_run is not available in this version")
        self._files = []
        plan = prepare_common(self.binding, input_doc, policy, roles, self._capabilities, provider=provider,
                              catalog=self.catalog, project=self.project, now=self.now,
                              settings=self.settings, submission_id=self.submission_id, skills=self.skills,
                              engine_decision=self.engine_decision)
        for path, text in self._files:  # nothing is written when the preparation was refused
            path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
        return plan

    def project(self, input_doc: dict, base: dict, manifest: dict, cap: dict, resolved: dict) -> dict:
        raise NotImplementedError

    def _write(self, name: str, text: str) -> str:
        """Queue a file under ``out``; returns its launch-plan path."""
        path = self.out / name
        self._files.append((path, text))
        return _relative(path)

    def run(self, launch_plan: dict) -> str:
        raise PortError("NOT_IMPLEMENTED", "run is not available in this version")

    def watch(self, run_id: str, after_seq: int | None = None) -> Iterator[dict]:
        raise PortError("NOT_IMPLEMENTED", "watch is not available in this version")

    def cancel(self, run_id: str) -> dict:
        raise PortError("NOT_IMPLEMENTED", "cancel is not available in this version")

    def resume(self, run_id: str) -> str:
        raise PortError("NOT_IMPLEMENTED", "resume is not available in this version")

    def results(self, run_id: str) -> dict:
        raise PortError("NOT_IMPLEMENTED", "results is not available in this version")

    try:
        doc = adhoc.build_adhoc_input(args.goal, args.include or [], args.exclude or [], args.check or [],
                                      args.procedure or [], args.read or [], route=route, review=args.review,
                                      why=args.why, expect=args.expect)
    except adhoc.AdhocError as error:
        print(f"{error.code}: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2 if error.code == "USAGE" else 1
    print(json.dumps(doc, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))
    return 0


def _render_prompt(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    try:
        doc = json.loads(args.input.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        issues = [issue for issue in validate(doc, "execution-input") if issue.level == "error"]
        if issues:
            for issue in issues:
                print(f"{issue.code}: {issue.path or '/'} {issue.message}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
        manifest, text = render.load_role(args.role, args.roles_dir)
        sys.stdout.write(render.render_prompt(doc, manifest, text))
    except (OSError, ValueError) as error:
        print(f"INPUT_INVALID: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    except render.RenderError as error:
        print(f"{error.code}: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    return 0


def _load_json(path: Path) -> dict:
    try:
        return json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except (OSError, ValueError) as error:
        raise PortError("INPUT_INVALID", f"cannot read {path}: {error}") from error


def _load_skills(path: Path | None) -> dict | None:
    """``--skills FILE``: ``{role_id: [{name, digest}]}``, the output of the skill bridge for every role."""
    if path is None:
        return None
    found = _load_json(path)
    if not all(isinstance(role, str) and isinstance(items, list) for role, items in found.items()):
        raise PortError("INPUT_INVALID", f"{path} must map role ids to lists of {{name, digest}}")
    return found


def _primary_role(policy: dict) -> str:
    """The role whose engine setting chooses the engine of the run: the primary stage's role."""
    stages = policy.get("stages") if isinstance(policy, dict) else None
    for stage in stages if isinstance(stages, list) else []:
        if isinstance(stage, dict) and stage.get("kind") == "primary" and isinstance(stage.get("role"), str):
            return stage["role"]
    return "executor"


def _prepare(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    try:
        if not args.dry_run:
            raise PortError("NOT_IMPLEMENTED", "prepare only supports --dry-run in this version")
        input_doc, policy = _load_json(args.input), _load_json(args.policy)
        current = settings.load(project=_project_root(), config_file=args.config)  # the configuration is read once
        binding, decision = settings.select_engine(current, _primary_role(policy), flag=args.binding)
        roles = render.load_roles(args.roles_dir)
        engine = BINDINGS[binding](args.out, catalog=catalog.Catalog.load(args.model_catalog),
                                   roles_dir=args.roles_dir, settings=current, submission_id=args.submission_id,
                                   skills=_load_skills(args.skills), engine_decision=decision)
        plan = engine.prepare(input_doc, policy, roles, provider=args.provider, dry_run=True)
    except PortError as error:
        print(f"{error.code}: {error.message}", file=sys.stderr)
        for issue in error.data.get("issues", []):
            print(f"  {issue['code']}: {issue['path'] or '/'} {issue['message']}", file=sys.stderr)
        if "launch_plan" in error.data:  # the refusal report
            print(json.dumps(error.data["launch_plan"], ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))
        return 1
    except (catalog.CatalogError, launch.LaunchError, settings.SettingsError) as error:
        print(f"{error.code}: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    except ConfigError as error:
        print(f"CONFIG_INVALID: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    except (OSError, ValueError) as error:  # an unreadable role manifest
        print(f"INPUT_INVALID: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    print(json.dumps(plan, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))
    return 0


def _explanation(plan: dict) -> dict:
    """The parts of a launch-plan that say what was decided and why."""
    return {"binding": plan["binding"], "decisions": plan.get("decisions", []), "stages": plan["stages"],
            "refusals": plan["refusals"], "digests": plan.get("digests", {}), "config": plan.get("config", {}),
            "policy_decision": plan.get("policy_decision"), "warnings": plan.get("proof", {}).get("warnings", [])}


def _explain_text(found: dict) -> str:
    lines = []
    engine = next((item for item in found["decisions"] if item["kind"] == "binding"), None)
    why = ", ".join(code for item in (engine or {}).get("considered", []) if item["accepted"]
                    for code in item.get("reason_codes", []))
    lines.append(f"engine: {found['binding']}" + (f" ({why})" if why else ""))
    for item in (engine or {}).get("considered", []):
        if not item["accepted"]:
            lines.append(f"  not chosen: {item['candidate']} ({', '.join(item.get('reason_codes', []))})")
    lines.append("stages:")
    for stage in found["stages"]:
        parts = [stage.get("provider", "-"), stage.get("model", "-"), stage.get("effort", "-")]
        lines.append(f"  {stage['stage_id']}: role {stage['role']}, {', '.join(parts)}")
    if not found["stages"]:
        lines.append("  (none prepared)")
    lines.append("considered:")
    for decision in (item for item in found["decisions"] if item["kind"] != "binding"):
        lines.append(f"  {decision['stage_id']}: chosen {decision['chosen']}"
                     + (f" (tie-break {decision['tie_break']})" if "tie_break" in decision else ""))
        for item in decision["considered"]:
            verdict = "accepted" if item["accepted"] else "refused"
            codes = ", ".join(item.get("reason_codes", []))
            lines.append(f"    {item['candidate']}: {verdict}" + (f" ({codes})" if codes else ""))
    lines.append("refusals:")
    for item in found["refusals"]:
        lines.append(f"  {item['stage_id']}: {item['capability']}: {item['reason']}"
                     + (f" [{item['reason_code']}]" if "reason_code" in item else ""))
        for link in item.get("chain", []):
            lines.append(f"    because {link['capability']}: {link['reason']}")
    if not found["refusals"]:
        lines.append("  (none)")
    lines.append("digests:")
    for name, value in found["digests"].items():
        lines.append(f"  {name}: {value}")
    lines.append(f"config {found['config'].get('digest', '-')}:")
    for key, value in found["config"].get("values", {}).items():
        lines.append(f"  {key} = {json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False)}")
    decision = found["policy_decision"] or {}
    codes = ", ".join(decision.get("reason_codes", []))
    lines.append(f"policy decision: {decision.get('decision', '-')}" + (f" ({codes})" if codes else ""))
    lines.append("warnings:")
    lines.extend(f"  {item['code']}: {item['message']}" for item in found["warnings"])
    if not found["warnings"]:
        lines.append("  (none)")
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def _explain(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    """Read-only: validates the launch-plan, prints why it looks the way it does, writes nothing."""
    try:
        plan = _load_json(args.file)
    except PortError as error:
        print(f"{error.code}: {error.message}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    issues = [issue for issue in validate(plan, "launch-plan") if issue.level == "error"]
    if issues:
        for issue in issues:
            print(f"{issue.code}: {issue.path or '/'} {issue.message}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    found = _explanation(plan)
    if args.json:
        print(json.dumps(found, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))
    else:
        sys.stdout.write(_explain_text(found))
    return 0


def _project_root() -> Path | None:
    """The project the working directory belongs to: a git repository or a folder with ``.swissknifeman``."""
    from aicore.state import find_project_root
    root = find_project_root(Path.cwd())
    return root if (root / ".git").exists() or (root / ".swissknifeman").is_dir() else None


def _policy(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    try:
        current = settings.load(project=_project_root(), config_file=args.config)
        if args.action == "list":
            rows = [policies.describe(policy_id, current) for policy_id in policies.discover(current)]
            if args.json:
                print(json.dumps(rows, ensure_ascii=False))
            else:
                for row in rows:
                    print(f"{row['policy_id']}\t{row['version']}\t{row['cases']} cases\t{row['source']}\t{row['description']}")
        elif args.action == "show":
            print(json.dumps(policies.load(args.policy_id, current), ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))
        else:
            ids = args.policy_id or list(policies.discover(current))
            rows = [row for policy_id in ids for row in policies.run_cases(policy_id, current)]
            if args.json:
                print(json.dumps(rows, ensure_ascii=False))
            else:
                for row in rows:
                    print(f"{row['status'].upper()}\t{row['policy_id']}\t{row['case'] or '-'}")
                    for item in row["differences"]:
                        print(f"  {item['field']}: expected {json.dumps(item['expected'], ensure_ascii=False)}, "
                              f"got {json.dumps(item['actual'], ensure_ascii=False)}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1 if any(row["status"] != "pass" for row in rows) else 0
    except policies.PolicyError as error:
        print(f"{error.code}: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
        for issue in error.issues:
            print(f"  {issue['code']}: {issue['path'] or '/'} {issue['message']}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    except ConfigError as error:
        print(f"CONFIG_INVALID: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    except settings.SettingsError as error:
        print(f"{error.code}: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    return 0


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="orch.py")
    parser.add_argument("--config", type=Path, metavar="FILE", help="configuration file of the invocation layer")

    for sub in (show, build):

    build.add_argument("--effort")
    build.add_argument("--cwd", default=".")
    command = verbs.add_parser("input", help="create an execution-input without a plan")
    command = command.add_subparsers(dest="kind", required=True).add_parser(
        "adhoc", help="ad-hoc input, or a read-only review with --review BASE..HEAD")
    command.add_argument("--goal")
    command.add_argument("--why")
    command.add_argument("--include", nargs="+", action="extend")
    command.add_argument("--exclude", nargs="+", action="extend")
    command.add_argument("--check", action="append", metavar="V1=CMD", help="command check, expects exit 0")
    command.add_argument("--procedure", action="append", metavar="V2=TEXT", help="manual check, expects observed")
    command.add_argument("--expect", help="expected outcome of every --check (default: exit 0)")
    command.add_argument("--read", nargs="+", action="extend", metavar="PATH")
    command.add_argument("--class", dest="model_class", choices=("economy", "implementation", "frontier"))
    command.add_argument("--effort", choices=("low", "medium", "high", "xhigh", "max", "ultra"))
    command.add_argument("--review", metavar="BASE..HEAD")
    command = verbs.add_parser("render-prompt", help="role prompt for a Claude-only run (Markdown)")
    command.add_argument("--input", type=Path, required=True)
    command.add_argument("--role", required=True)
    command.add_argument("--roles-dir", type=Path)
    command = verbs.add_parser("prepare", help="launch-plan of a run; --dry-run writes projection files only")
    command.add_argument("--binding", choices=sorted(BINDINGS),
                         help="engine; without it the [orch] configuration chooses (engine_by_role, engine)")
    command.add_argument("--provider")
    command.add_argument("--input", type=Path, required=True)
    command.add_argument("--policy", type=Path, required=True)
    command.add_argument("--out", type=Path, required=True, help="directory for prompts and profiles")
    command.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
    command.add_argument("--model-catalog", type=Path, dest="model_catalog", metavar="FILE",
                         help="model-catalog/v1 file (default: the catalog packaged with aicore)")
    command.add_argument("--roles-dir", type=Path)
    command.add_argument("--submission-id", dest="submission_id", metavar="ID",
                         help="submission the launch-plan belongs to; must differ from the run id")
    command.add_argument("--skills", type=Path, metavar="FILE",
                         help="JSON {role_id: [{name, digest}]}: skills delivered per role (skill bridge output)")
    command = verbs.add_parser("explain", help="why a launch-plan looks as it does (read-only)")
    command.add_argument("file", type=Path)
    command.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    command = verbs.add_parser("policy", help="run-policy packs: list, show, test")
    actions = command.add_subparsers(dest="action", required=True)
    listing = actions.add_parser("list", help="every pack with version, case count and source")
    listing.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    show = actions.add_parser("show", help="the run-policy of a pack as JSON")
    show.add_argument("policy_id")
    test = actions.add_parser("test", help="run the cases of packs (all packs without an id)")
    test.add_argument("policy_id", nargs="*")
    test.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if args.verb == "policy":
        return _policy(args)
    if args.verb == "launch":
        return _launch(args)
    if args.verb == "input":
        return _input_adhoc(args)
    if args.verb == "render-prompt":
        return _render_prompt(args)
    if args.verb == "prepare":
        return _prepare(args)
    if args.verb == "explain":
        return _explain(args)
    try:
        doc = json.loads(args.file.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
        print(f"INPUT_INVALID: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    try:

    if not args.quiet:
        result = [issue._asdict() for issue in issues]

I am beginning a thorough review of the code against its contract.

I am checking the eight contract requirements. Determinism depends on stable stage ordering in the policy.

The `ready` list preserves original stage order, so it is stable if the input policy is ordered. `proof`, `warnings`, and `capabilities` are all sorted before hashing. However, `roles` is converted to a dict via `dict(roles)`, which means digest determinism depends on the caller's key insertion order.

`config["values"]` ordering from `orch_settings.affecting` is unverified. `modules` order is fixed. `decisions` ordering depends on `select_engine`'s `considered` sequence, which may be unstable. `blocked` preserves insertion order of reason codes and is deterministic. `created_at` uses `datetime.now()` without a `now` argument, so it is not deterministic.

The CLI does not pass `now` to the engine constructor. This confirms `datetime.now()` is used and the digest is non-deterministic.

The missing `--now` flag is acceptable because the contract treats `now` as an explicit argument. The CLI omits it, so wall-clock time becomes part of the input and produces different digests across runs.

`_relative` uses `os.path.relpath(path, Path.cwd())`, so capability paths depend on the current working directory. Running from different directories changes the plan bytes, which may violate the contract if CWD is not treated as an input.

The `_relative` path issue may be pre-existing and outside the changed scope. I am checking whether `config.digest` includes home-dependent paths from `affecting()`. Warnings keyed by provider overwrite duplicates deterministically. Skills order is stable because it follows the input file.

I am now examining the stale capability logic. The code checks `is_stale` before calling `_stage_requirements`, and if the capability is stale it appends a `CAPABILITY_STALE` reason code and issues a warning. The `_stage_requirements` function also raises an `Unmet` error when `refuse_stale` is true and the capability is stale. The `is_stale` check compares the capability's `fresh_until` timestamp against the current time.

I am analyzing the `_moment` timestamp truncation. It strips fractional seconds and timezone information, so two timestamps that differ only in sub-second precision collapse to identical values. This means a capability fresh until `.5Z` and one fresh until `.999Z` in the same second are treated as equal, which could affect stale checks.

I found a bug in the stale capability warning logic. The stale warning is only recorded when `_stage_requirements` succeeds. If another requirement fails first, the stale warning is skipped entirely. This means a stale capability can be silently ignored when it should be flagged.

The contract explicitly forbids silently accepting stale capabilities. The proof entry still records `stale: True` regardless of whether the warning is emitted, so the missing warning is a real defect.

The stale flag is written to the proof before any requirement checks. If a stage fails for a different reason, the capability is not accepted and the warning may be unnecessary. In warn mode, the stage is still accepted with a warning.

I confirmed that warnings are stored once per provider even when multiple stages share it. The `created` timestamp is consistently truncated by `_moment` whether `now` is passed explicitly or generated internally. An unformatted or timezone-less `now` string would raise an uncaught `ValueError` inside `_moment`. The stale comparison logic appears sound for Zulu timestamps.

The sub-second boundary behavior is intentional. The docstring explicitly states that optional fractions are stripped, so stale checks operate at second resolution. This is not a defect.

`orch.port` is the boundary between the engine-neutral [exec/v1 contracts](contracts.md) and the
engine bindings `native`, `cao` and `claude-only` (`BINDINGS`). It holds the protocol, its errors
and the `RunState` reducer, with the retry table, the run journal and the effect check in `orch.retry`, `orch.journal` and `orch.effects`; `prepare_common` and the bindings are in `orch.bindings`, the resume guard in `orch.resume`.

Invariant: one run has one workflow owner. A binding never calls another binding; the CAO adapter does
not start the native engine; Claude-only is a human or Claude session that receives a prompt and
returns a report.
10→
## Operations

`EnginePort` is a `runtime_checkable` `typing.Protocol`:

| Operation | Returns | Plan 1 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `binding` | `"native"`, `"cao"` or `"claude-only"` | attribute |
| `capabilities()` | capability-record list (`declared` or `probed`) | seeds |
| `prepare(input_doc, policy, roles, *, provider=None, dry_run=True)` | launch-plan | dry run only |
20→| `run(launch_plan)` | run id | `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` |
| `watch(run_id, after_seq=None)` | iterator of run-events with `seq > after_seq` (all when `None`) | `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` |
| `cancel(run_id)` | `{"run_id", "cancelled": [stage_id], "unknown": [stage_id]}` | `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` |
| `resume(run_id)` | run id, or `RESUME_REFUSED` | `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` |
| `results(run_id)` | `{"stage_results": [...], "effect_receipts": [...]}` | `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` |

## Prepare

`prepare_common(binding, input_doc, policy, roles, capabilities, *, provider, catalog, project=None, now=None,
settings=None, submission_id=None, skills=None, model_catalog_doc=None, launch_catalog_doc=None,
30→engine_decision=None)` is the algorithm every binding shares; the new arguments are optional. It validates the
input, policy and role manifests, orders stages by `depends_on`, enforces the minimum route of the primary stage and
matches each model stage (`scout`, `primary`, `bounded`, `review`, `condense`) against the `(binding, provider)`
capability record. Models resolve only through the model catalog of aicore (`--model-catalog`). The result is a
function of the arguments and `now`: the same inputs give the same bytes.

1. `digests`: `input`, `policy` (`canonical_digest`), `roles` (canonical JSON of the manifests by role id),
   `launch_catalog`, `model_catalog`, `capabilities` (canonical JSON of the records of this binding by
   `<binding>--<provider>`, without `_path`) and `config`.
2. `config` is the snapshot of the `[orch]` values that influence preparation (`settings.affecting`) with its digest;
40→   without `settings` the schema defaults are used. `modules` lists `aicore` and `orch` with their versions.
3. For each model stage the candidate is the stage provider, else the `provider` argument. The candidate is checked
   against the requirements below and for freshness. `decisions` gets `{stage_id, kind: "route", chosen, considered,
   tie_break: "policy-order"}`; `chosen` is `<provider>/<model>` (the class when the binding cannot select a model),
   or `none` when the stage was refused.
4. A record is stale when `fresh_until` is before `now`. With `capabilities.stale = "warn"` the candidate stays
   acceptable with the reason code `CAPABILITY_STALE` and `proof.warnings` names it; with `"refuse"` the stage is refused.
5. Every refusal has a `reason_code` and a `chain`: the requested capability and its reason, then each capability named
   by the record's `depends_on` that is itself unavailable.
6. The engine decision (kind `binding`, stage `*`) is `engine_decision` from `settings.select_engine`; without it the
50→   caller named the engine (`ENGINE_FROM_FLAG`). A missing capability never switches the engine: the stage is refused.
7. `policy_decision` is `allow`, or `refuse` with the reason codes of the refused `required` stages;
   `policy_digest` is `digests.policy`.
8. `submission_id`, when given, is recorded; `KEY_REUSED` refuses one equal to the run id. `skills` (`{role_id:
   [{name, digest}]}`, the output of the skill bridge) fills `stages[].delivery.skills`. `proof` (dry run) snapshots
   the records that were used: `binding`, `provider`, `source`, `observed_at` (the record's `recorded_at` when it names
   no `observed_at`), `fresh_until`, `stale`.
9. `digest` of the plan is computed last.

| Reason code | Requirement |
60→| --- | --- |
| `CAP_RECORD_MISSING` | no capability record for `(binding, provider)` |
| `CAPABILITY_STALE` | the record is past `fresh_until` and `capabilities.stale` is `refuse` (a warning otherwise) |
| `MODEL_SET_UNKNOWN`, `MODEL_SET_UNSUPPORTED` | the binding cannot guarantee or select a model |
| `SKILL_DELIVERY_UNAVAILABLE` | required skills cannot be delivered |
| `INDEPENDENT_PROVIDER` | a review would run on the primary provider |
| `READ_ONLY_UNENFORCEABLE` | a read-only role cannot be enforced |
| `CATALOG_UNKNOWN` | the model catalog has no class or effort entry |
| `LAUNCH_UNKNOWN`, `LAUNCH_INVALID`, `LAUNCH_MODEL_UNSETTABLE` | the launch catalog cannot start the role with a model |

70→An unmet requirement of a `required` stage raises `CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED` with the plan as `data.launch_plan`; an
optional stage becomes a refusal. Provider and model are never replaced silently.

`orch.py prepare [--binding B] [--provider P] --input I --policy POLICY --out DIR --dry-run [--submission-id ID]
[--skills FILE] [--model-catalog FILE]` reads the `[orch]` configuration once (`--config` is the invocation layer).
Without `--binding` the engine is `engine_by_role[<role of the primary stage>]`, else `engine`; the flag wins. Prepare
without `--dry-run` stays `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`.

`orch.py explain LAUNCH_PLAN [--json]` validates a launch-plan (exit 1 when invalid) and prints the engine and why, each
stage with provider, model and effort, the candidates considered with reason codes, the refusals with their chain, the
80→digests, the configuration values, the policy decision and the warnings. `--json` prints `{binding, decisions, stages,
refusals, digests, config, policy_decision, warnings}`. It writes nothing.

`orch.resume.verify_resume(plan, *, input_digest, policy_digest, roles_digest, config_digest, binding)` returns the
names of the inputs that differ from the launch-plan (`input`, `policy`, `roles`, `config`, `binding`, in that order);
an empty list allows resume. A plan that did not record a value counts as drifted. The future `resume` refuses with
`RESUME_REFUSED` and `data.drift`.

`RunState.stage_result(..., skills=None, modules=None, attempt_id=None, owner_epoch=None)` carries the skills that
took part, the module versions, the attempt and the owner epoch into the stage-result.
90→
## Errors

`PortError(code, message, data=None)` exposes `code`, `message` and `data`; a code outside
`PORT_ERROR_CODES` is a programming error (`ValueError`). The table order is the tuple order.

| Code | When |
| --- | --- |
| `INPUT_INVALID` | execution-input or run-event fails the schema or semantic checks; a stage event is inconsistent |
| `POLICY_INVALID` | run-policy fails the schema or semantic checks |
100→| `ROLE_UNKNOWN` | a stage refers to a role without a manifest |
| `ROUTE_UNDERSHOOT` | the primary stage class is below `input.route.minimum.class` |
| `CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED` | a `required` stage needs an `unsupported` or `unknown` capability; `data.launch_plan` holds the report |
| `RESUME_REFUSED` | input, policy, roles or config digests, or the binding, drifted before resume (`data.drift`, see `verify_resume`) |
| `RUN_UNKNOWN` | unknown run id, or an event of another run |
| `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` | an execution operation in Plan 1 (`run`, `watch`, `cancel`, `resume`, `results`, `prepare(dry_run=False)`) |
| `SEQ_ORDER` | reducer: `seq` repeated with other content, or lower than the last seen |
| `AFTER_TERMINAL` | reducer: an event of an attempt that already ended, or a retry after `completed`/`cancelled` |
| `EVENT_CONFLICT` | reducer, journal: an `event_id` repeated with different content |
| `STALE_EPOCH` | reducer: an `owner_epoch` lower than the highest one seen; the writer lost the run |
110→
## States

`RunState(run_id)` folds run-events without I/O or the system clock; every value comes from events.
An event is fully checked before any change, so a rejected event leaves the state untouched.
Retained event data is copied: modifying an event after `apply()` cannot change the reduced result.

- `apply(event)` checks in a fixed order and changes nothing before every check passed:
  1. an event of another `contract_version` is kept (`foreign()` returns copies) and not applied;
  2. schema (`INPUT_INVALID`) and `run_id` (`RUN_UNKNOWN`);
120→  3. identity: with `event_id` the key is the id — an identical replay is ignored, other content is
     `EVENT_CONFLICT`; then `seq` — an identical replay is ignored, other content under a seen `seq` or a
     lower `seq` is `SEQ_ORDER`. Gaps are allowed;
  4. fencing: an `owner_epoch` lower than the highest seen is `STALE_EPOCH`; an event without
     `owner_epoch` is not fenced;
  5. the stage rules of the table below. A normalized `error` (error/v1) of the event is copied into the
     stage error record as `error`.
- `close()` ends the stream: a `running` stage becomes `unknown_outcome` with error
  `{class: transport, message: "stream ended without terminal event"}`. End of stream is never success.
- `stages()` returns copies: `stage_id → {status, attempt, last_seq, last_ts, route_observed, errors}`.
130→- `stage_result(stage_id, *, role, requested_route, input_digest, instructions_digest)` builds a
  schema-valid skeleton stage-result of the latest attempt; a running or unknown stage is `INPUT_INVALID`.

| Event kind | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `started` | `running`. Attempt 1 for a new stage; attempt `prev + 1` after `failed`, `timeout`, `quota_blocked`, `auth_blocked` or `unknown_outcome`; errors and usage start empty |
| `model_wait`, `output`, `tool`, `question`, `check` | status unchanged; `last_ts` moves (silence timeout) |
| `provider_error` | status unchanged; adds error class `provider` |
| `quota_block` | terminal `quota_blocked`, error class `quota` — not a task failure |
| `auth_block` | terminal `auth_blocked`, error class `auth` — not a task failure |
140→| `timeout` | terminal `timeout`, error class `timeout` |
| `cancelled`, `failed`, `unknown_outcome` | terminal status of the same name |
| `completed` | terminal `completed`; usage from its `data.usage` |

A stage accepts only `started` before its first attempt; an event for a later attempt that has not
started is `INPUT_INVALID`. Any new event for an ended attempt, including a delayed `started`, is
`AFTER_TERMINAL`; an identical replay is still ignored. `route_observed` from any event becomes
`route.observed` with `source: "event"`. Usage is `{"status": "reported"}` with integer `input_tokens`/`output_tokens` taken
from the last `completed.data.usage`, otherwise `{"status": "unknown"}` without numbers.

150→## Retry decisions

`orch.retry` is a pure function of the failure class, the stage state and the run policy; the class comes
from an error/v1 record or the terminal event kind (`class_of`), never from message text.
`decide(RetryInputs, policy)` returns `RetryDecision(action, reason_codes, wait_s, route)` with the action
`stop`, `retry`, `retry_after`, `fallback_route`, `replan` or `reconcile`. Rules, in order:

1. the action is `policy.on_error[class].action` (`ACTION_FROM_POLICY`) or `DEFAULT_ACTIONS[class]`
   (`ACTION_DEFAULT`): authentication, authorization, invalid_request, content_policy and unknown stop;
   quota and rate_limit retry after a wait; model_unavailable, provider_internal, transport and timeout
160→   retry; context_limit replans; unknown_outcome reconciles;
2. `unknown_outcome` of a writing stage is always `reconcile` (`UNKNOWN_OUTCOME_WRITE`); of a read-only
   stage it follows the policy or retries (`UNKNOWN_OUTCOME_READ_ONLY`);
3. a repeating action (`retry`, `retry_after`, `fallback_route`) of a writing stage with a dirty worktree
   or an unresolved receipt becomes `reconcile` (`PARTIAL_CHANGES`);
4. a repeating action is `stop` (`BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`) when `attempts_used` (including the failed one)
   exceeds the stage `retries.max` or the policy `max` of the class, or `budget_left` is zero;
5. `retry_after` waits `retry_after_s`; without it quota stops (`RETRY_AFTER_UNKNOWN`) and the other
   classes wait `RATE_LIMIT_DEFAULT_WAIT_S`;
6. `fallback_route` takes the first of `policy.fallback_routes` that differs from the current route
170→   (`FALLBACK_ROUTE`; the caller emits the event that explains the switch), else `stop`
   (`FALLBACK_UNDECLARED`); a provider or model never changes without this decision;
7. `replan` carries `CONTEXT_LIMIT`.

## Run journal

`orch.journal` is the only module that writes the files of a run: `<state>/orch/runs/<run_id>/` holds
`events.jsonl`, `events.lock`, `run.json`, `launch-plan.json` and `receipts/<n>.json` (state of the project
when a project is given, else the machine state; directories `0700`, files `0600`).

180→- `append_event(dir, event)` validates the run-event, takes an exclusive `flock` on `events.lock`, and
  appends one canonical JSON line. An identical event (same `event_id`, or same `seq`) returns `False`
  without a write; other content under the same `event_id` is `EVENT_CONFLICT`, under the same `seq`
  `SEQ_ORDER`. A torn last line (a crash) stays a broken line of its own; the next event starts on a new line.
- `read_events(dir, after_seq=None)` yields complete lines with `seq > after_seq` in file order and skips an
  unfinished or broken line; the same call gives the same sequence. This is the cursor of `watch`.
- `write_doc` / `read_doc` replace a document atomically (temporary file, then `os.replace`); a document
  that was not written reads as `None`.

## Effects
190→
`orch.effects` re-checks the precondition right before an effect. `check(...)` returns a `Verdict`:
a receipt of the same `effect_key` with outcome `applied` or `already_applied` gives `already_applied`
and no execution; an `unknown` receipt gives no verdict to run (the caller reconciles through
`retry.decide`); an observed prior state that differs from `intent.expected_prior` gives a `failed`
receipt with `precondition.matched = false` and reason `PRECONDITION_CHANGED`; otherwise the effect may run
and `record(outcome="applied", observed_prior=...)` follows. Receipts are checked against `effect-receipt`;
no function here reads the clock or the disk.

## Adding an engine

## States

`RunState(run_id)` folds run-events without I/O or the system clock; every value comes from events.
An event is fully checked before any change, so a rejected event leaves the state untouched.
Retained event data is copied: modifying an event after `apply()` cannot change the reduced result.

- `apply(event)` checks in a fixed order and changes nothing before every check passed:
  1. an event of another `contract_version` is kept (`foreign()` returns copies) and not applied;
  2. schema (`INPUT_INVALID`) and `run_id` (`RUN_UNKNOWN`);
120→  3. identity: with `event_id` the key is the id — an identical replay is ignored, other content is
     `EVENT_CONFLICT`; then `seq` — an identical replay is ignored, other content under a seen `seq` or a
     lower `seq` is `SEQ_ORDER`. Gaps are allowed;
  4. fencing: an `owner_epoch` lower than the highest seen is `STALE_EPOCH`; an event without
     `owner_epoch` is not fenced;
  5. the stage rules of the table below. A normalized `error` (error/v1) of the event is copied into the
     stage error record as `error`.

130→- `stage_result(stage_id, *, role, requested_route, input_digest, instructions_digest)` builds a

| Event kind | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `started` | `running`. Attempt 1 for a new stage; attempt `prev + 1` after `failed`, `timeout`, `quota_blocked`, `auth_blocked` or `unknown_outcome`; errors and usage start empty |

| `auth_block` | terminal `auth_blocked`, error class `auth` — not a task failure |
140→| `timeout` | terminal `timeout`, error class `timeout` |

started is `INPUT_INVALID`. Any new event for an ended attempt, including a delayed `started`, is

150→## Retry decisions

`orch.retry` is a pure function of the failure class, the stage state and the run policy; the class comes
from an error/v1 record or the terminal event kind (`class_of`), never from message text.
`decide(RetryInputs, policy)` returns `RetryDecision(action, reason_codes, wait_s, route)` with the action
`stop`, `retry`, `retry_after`, `fallback_route`, `replan` or `reconcile`. Rules, in order:

1. the action is `policy.on_error[class].action` (`ACTION_FROM_POLICY`) or `DEFAULT_ACTIONS[class]`
   (`ACTION_DEFAULT`): authentication, authorization, invalid_request, content_policy and unknown stop;
   quota and rate_limit retry after a wait; model_unavailable, provider_internal, transport and timeout
160→   retry; context_limit replans; unknown_outcome reconciles;
2. `unknown_outcome` of a writing stage is always `reconcile` (`UNKNOWN_OUTCOME_WRITE`); of a read-only
   stage it follows the policy or retries (`UNKNOWN_OUTCOME_READ_ONLY`);
3. a repeating action (`retry`, `retry_after`, `fallback_route`) of a writing stage with a dirty worktree
   or an unresolved receipt becomes `reconcile` (`PARTIAL_CHANGES`);
4. a repeating action is `stop` (`BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`) when `attempts_used` (including the failed one)
   exceeds the stage `retries.max` or the policy `max` of the class, or `budget_left` is zero;
5. `retry_after` waits `retry_after_s`; without it quota stops (`RETRY_AFTER_UNKNOWN`) and the other
   classes wait `RATE_LIMIT_DEFAULT_WAIT_S`;
6. `fallback_route` takes the first of `policy.fallback_routes` that differs from the current route
170→   (`FALLBACK_ROUTE`; the caller emits the event that explains the switch), else `stop`
   (`FALLBACK_UNDECLARED`); a provider or model never changes without this decision;

## Run journal

`orch.journal` is the only module that writes the files of a run: `<state>/orch/runs/<run_id>/` holds
`events.jsonl`, `events.lock`, `run.json`, `launch-plan.json` and `receipts/<n>.json` (state of the project
when a project is given, else the machine state; directories `0700`, files `0600`).

180→- `append_event(dir, event)` validates the run-event, takes an exclusive `flock` on `events.lock`, and

  without a write; other content under the same `event_id` is `EVENT_CONFLICT`, under the same `seq`
  `SEQ_ORDER`. A torn last line (a crash) stays a broken line of its own; the next event starts on a new line.
- `read_events(dir, after_seq=None)` yields complete lines with `seq > after_seq` in file order and skips an
  unfinished or broken line; the same call gives the same sequence. This is the cursor of `watch`.
- `write_doc` / `read_doc` replace a document atomically (temporary file, then `os.replace`); a document
  that was not written reads as `None`.

## Effects
190→
`orch.effects` re-checks the precondition right before an effect. `check(...)` returns a `Verdict`:
a receipt of the same `effect_key` with outcome `applied` or `already_applied` gives `already_applied`
and no execution; an `unknown` receipt gives no verdict to run (the caller reconciles through
`retry.decide`); an observed prior state that differs from `intent.expected_prior` gives a `failed`
receipt with `precondition.matched = false` and reason `PRECONDITION_CHANGED`; otherwise the effect may run
and `record(outcome="applied", observed_prior=...)` follows. Receipts are checked against `effect-receipt`;
no function here reads the clock or the disk.

- `apply(event)` checks in a fixed order and changes nothing before every check passed:
  1. an event of another `contract_version` is kept (`foreign()` returns copies) and not applied;
  2. schema (`INPUT_INVALID`) and `run_id` (`RUN_UNKNOWN`);
  3. identity: with `event_id` the key is the id — an identical replay is ignored, other content is
     `EVENT_CONFLICT`; then `seq` — an identical replay is ignored, other content under a seen `seq` or a
     lower `seq` is `SEQ_ORDER`. Gaps are allowed;
  4. fencing: an `owner_epoch` lower than the highest seen is `STALE_EPOCH`; an event without
     `owner_epoch` is not fenced;
  5. the stage rules of the table below. A normalized `error` (error/v1) of the event is copied into the
     stage error record as `error`.
- `close()` ends the stream: a `running` stage becomes `unknown_outcome` with error
  `{class: transport, message: "stream ended without terminal event"}`. End of stream is never success.
- `stages()` returns copies: `stage_id → {status, attempt, last_seq, last_ts, route_observed, errors}`.
- `stage_result(stage_id, *, role, requested_route, input_digest, instructions_digest)` builds a
  schema-valid skeleton stage-result of the latest attempt; a running or unknown stage is `INPUT_INVALID`.

| Event kind | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `started` | `running`. Attempt 1 for a new stage; attempt `prev + 1` after `failed`, `timeout`, `quota_blocked`, `auth_blocked` or `unknown_outcome`; errors and usage start empty |
| `model_wait`, `output`, `tool`, `question`, `check` | status unchanged; `last_ts` moves (silence timeout) |
| `provider_error` | status unchanged; adds error class `provider` |
| `quota_block` | terminal `quota_blocked`, error class `quota` — not a task failure |
| `auth_block` | terminal `auth_blocked`, error class `auth` — not a task failure |
| `timeout` | terminal `timeout`, error class `timeout` |
| `cancelled`, `failed`, `unknown_outcome` | terminal status of the same name |
| `completed` | terminal `completed`; usage from its `data.usage` |

A stage accepts only `started` before its first attempt; an event for a later attempt that has not
started is `INPUT_INVALID`. Any new event for an ended attempt, including a delayed `started`, is
`AFTER_TERMINAL`; an identical replay is still ignored. `route_observed` from any event becomes
`route.observed` with `source: "event"`. Usage is `{"status": "reported"}` with integer `input_tokens`/`output_tokens` taken
from the last `completed.data.usage`, otherwise `{"status": "unknown"}` without numbers.

## Retry decisions

`orch.retry` is a pure function of the failure class, the stage state and the run policy; the class comes
from an error/v1 record or the terminal event kind (`class_of`), never from message text.
`decide(RetryInputs, policy)` returns `RetryDecision(action, reason_codes, wait_s, route)` with the action
`stop`, `retry`, `retry_after`, `fallback_route`, `replan` or `reconcile`. Rules, in order:

1. the action is `policy.on_error[class].action` (`ACTION_FROM_POLICY`) or `DEFAULT_ACTIONS[class]`
   (`ACTION_DEFAULT`): authentication, authorization, invalid_request, content_policy and unknown stop;
   quota and rate_limit retry after a wait; model_unavailable, provider_internal, transport and timeout
   retry; context_limit replans; unknown_outcome reconciles;
2. `unknown_outcome` of a writing stage is always `reconcile` (`UNKNOWN_OUTCOME_WRITE`); of a read-only
   stage it follows the policy or retries (`UNKNOWN_OUTCOME_READ_ONLY`);
3. a repeating action (`retry`, `retry_after`, `fallback_route`) of a writing stage with a dirty worktree
   or an unresolved receipt becomes `reconcile` (`PARTIAL_CHANGES`);
4. a repeating action is `stop` (`BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`) when `attempts_used` (including the failed one)
   exceeds the stage `retries.max` or the policy `max` of the class, or `budget_left` is zero;
5. `retry_after` waits `retry_after_s`; without it quota stops (`RETRY_AFTER_UNKNOWN`) and the other
   classes wait `RATE_LIMIT_DEFAULT_WAIT_S`;
6. `fallback_route` takes the first of `policy.fallback_routes` that differs from the current route
   (`FALLBACK_ROUTE`; the caller emits the event that explains the switch), else `stop`
   (`FALLBACK_UNDECLARED`); a provider or model never changes without this decision;
7. `replan` carries `CONTEXT_LIMIT`.

## Run journal

`orch.journal` is the only module that writes the files of a run: `<state>/orch/runs/<run_id>/` holds
`events.jsonl`, `events.lock`, `run.json`, `launch-plan.json` and `receipts/<n>.json` (state of the project
when a project is given, else the machine state; directories `0700`, files `0600`).

- `append_event(dir, event)` validates the run-event, takes an exclusive `flock` on `events.lock`, and
  appends one canonical JSON line. An identical event (same `event_id`, or same `seq`) returns `False`
  without a write; other content under the same `event_id` is `EVENT_CONFLICT`, under the same `seq`
  `SEQ_ORDER`. A torn last line (a crash) stays a broken line of its own; the next event starts on a new line.
- `read_events(dir, after_seq=None)` yields complete lines with `seq > after_seq` in file order and skips an
  unfinished or broken line; the same call gives the same sequence. This is the cursor of `watch`.
- `write_doc` / `read_doc` replace a document atomically (temporary file, then `os.replace`); a document
  that was not written reads as `None`.

## Effects

`orch.effects` re-checks the precondition right before an effect. `check(...)` returns a `Verdict`:
a receipt of the same `effect_key` with outcome `applied` or `already_applied` gives `already_applied`
and no execution; an `unknown` receipt gives no verdict to run (the caller reconciles through
`retry.decide`); an observed prior state that differs from `intent.expected_prior` gives a `failed`
receipt with `precondition.matched = false` and reason `PRECONDITION_CHANGED`; otherwise the effect may run
and `record(outcome="applied", observed_prior=...)` follows. Receipts are checked against `effect-receipt`;
no function here reads the clock or the disk.

## Binding matrix

Data: [`bindings/matrix.json`](../bindings/matrix.json). Values: `supported`, `adapted`, `unsupported`,
`unknown`; `skill_delivery` uses capability-record `skill_delivery.mode` values. A native value refers to
the provider's main transport; `by_provider` overrides it per provider. Grok stays `unknown` until a
Plan 2 probe.

| Capability | native | cao | claude-only |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `prepare` | supported | supported (profile dry-render) | supported (prompt render) |
| `run` | supported (Plan 2) | adapted (`cao launch`, tmux) | adapted (session executes the prompt) |
| `watch` | supported (JSONL/ACP events) | adapted (TUI status; parse failure → `unknown_outcome`) | unsupported |
| `cancel` | supported for every provider (process group SIGTERM → SIGKILL) | adapted (`cao shutdown`) | unsupported |
| `resume` | adapted (session resume + hash check); grok unknown | adapted (workflow replay) | unsupported |
| `results` | supported | adapted (CAO response normalization) | adapted (report → stage-result) |
| `model_set` | supported (claude, codex `--model`); grok unknown | supported (profile `model`) | unsupported (session model) |
| `model_observe` | supported (claude `system/init`); codex adapted; grok unknown | adapted | adapted (report) |
| `effort_set` | supported (claude `--effort`, codex `model_reasoning_effort`); grok unknown | adapted (claude, codex); grok unsupported | unsupported |
| `skill_delivery` | claude `native_plugin_dir`; codex `isolated_home` (auth copied); grok unknown | `profile_skills` (advertised, not an ACL) | `project_dir` / `prompt_inline` |
| `tool_restrictions` | supported (claude `--tools`, codex `--sandbox`); grok unknown | adapted (`allowedTools`/role) | unsupported (prompt-only) |
| `plan_write_prevention` | adapted (tools + sandbox; shell can still write) | adapted | unsupported |
| `usage` | supported (claude `result`, codex `turn.completed`); grok unknown | unknown | unknown |
| `effects` | supported (receipts written by orch) | adapted (outside CAO memoization) | unsupported (registrar records) |
| `stream_live` | supported | adapted | unsupported |

## Adding an engine

1. Add the value to `defs.binding` (a minor exec/v1 change) and record it in the contract changelog.
2. Add `orch/bindings/<name>.py` implementing `EnginePort`; `prepare` calls `prepare_common`.
3. Add capability seeds `bindings/capabilities/<name>--<provider>.json` (`declared`, with evidence).
4. Add a column to `bindings/matrix.json` and to the table above; the matrix test requires every cell.
5. Add the binding to `BINDINGS`; the conformance test is parameterized by it.
6. Do not change the plan store, the skill catalog or the input, policy and role schemas: needing that is a contract defect.

def fixture(kind: str, name: str) -> dict:

def roles() -> dict:

def with_stage(policy: dict, **stage) -> dict:

class ProofCase(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.tmp.cleanup)
        self.out = Path(self.tmp.name) / "out"
        self.catalog = catalog.Catalog.load(MODEL_CATALOG)
        self.settings = settings.defaults()
        self.input = fixture("execution-input", "plan-bound")
        self.policy = fixture("run-policy", "solo")
        self.caps = load_capabilities()

    def primary_on(self, provider: str) -> dict:
        policy = copy.deepcopy(self.policy)
        next(stage for stage in policy["stages"] if stage["kind"] == "primary")["provider"] = provider
        return policy

    def prepare(self, binding="native", provider="claude-code", **kwargs) -> dict:
        input_doc, policy = kwargs.pop("input_doc", self.input), kwargs.pop("policy", self.policy)
        kwargs.setdefault("now", NOW)
        kwargs.setdefault("settings", self.settings)
        kwargs.setdefault("capabilities", self.caps)
        kwargs.setdefault("catalog", self.catalog)
        engine = BINDINGS[binding](self.out, **kwargs)
        return engine.prepare(input_doc, policy, roles(), provider=provider)

    def refusal(self, **kwargs) -> PortError:
        with self.assertRaises(PortError) as raised:
            self.prepare(**kwargs)
        return raised.exception

    def stale_caps(self) -> dict:
        caps = copy.deepcopy(self.caps)
        caps[("native", "claude-code")]["fresh_until"] = "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"
        return caps


class Determinism(ProofCase):
    def test_same_inputs_and_now_give_the_same_bytes(self):
        policy = with_stage(self.policy, id="scout", kind="scout", role="scout", required=False, on_unavailable="skip")
        first, second = self.prepare(policy=policy), self.prepare(policy=policy)
        self.assertEqual(json.dumps(first), json.dumps(second))
        self.assertEqual(json.dumps(first, sort_keys=True), json.dumps(second, sort_keys=True))
        self.assertEqual([d["stage_id"] for d in first["decisions"]], [d["stage_id"] for d in second["decisions"]])

    def test_plan_is_valid_and_its_digest_is_last(self):
        plan = self.prepare()
        self.assertEqual([i for i in contracts.validate(plan, "launch-plan") if i.level == "error"], [])
        self.assertEqual(list(plan)[-1], "digest")
        self.assertEqual(plan["digest"], contracts.canonical_digest(plan))

    def test_modules_and_default_config(self):
        plan = self.prepare(settings=None)
        self.assertEqual(plan["modules"], [{"id": "aicore", "version": aicore.__version__},
                                           {"id": "orch", "version": orch.__version__}])
        self.assertEqual(plan["config"]["digest"], settings.digest(settings.defaults()))
        self.assertEqual(plan["digests"]["config"], plan["config"]["digest"])

    def test_every_input_has_its_digest(self):
        plan = self.prepare()
        digests = plan["digests"]
        self.assertEqual(digests["input"], self.input["digest"])
        self.assertEqual(digests["policy"], contracts.canonical_digest(self.policy))
        self.assertEqual(set(digests), {"input", "policy", "roles", "launch_catalog", "model_catalog", "capabilities",
                                        "config"})
        self.assertEqual(plan["policy_decision"]["policy_digest"], digests["policy"])

    def test_a_changed_input_changes_only_its_digest(self):
        base = self.prepare()["digests"]
        caps = copy.deepcopy(self.caps)
        caps[("native", "codex")]["cli"]["name"] = "codex-next"
        launch_doc = copy.deepcopy(self.catalog.launch)
        launch_doc["launch"]["executor"]["codex"]["timeout_s"] += 1
        other = copy.deepcopy(self.catalog.model_document())
        other["catalog_version"] = "9.9.9"
        for name, kwargs in (("capabilities", {"capabilities": caps}), ("launch_catalog", {"launch_catalog_doc": launch_doc}),
                             ("model_catalog", {"model_catalog_doc": other})):
            with self.subTest(name=name):
                changed = self._digests(**kwargs)
                self.assertEqual([key for key in base if base[key] != changed[key]], [name])
        policy = copy.deepcopy(self.policy)
        policy["description"] = "other"
        self.assertEqual([key for key, value in self._digests(policy=policy).items() if base[key] != value], ["policy"])

    def _digests(self, **kwargs) -> dict:
        from orch.bindings import prepare_common
        policy = kwargs.pop("policy", self.policy)
        caps = kwargs.pop("capabilities", self.caps)
        return prepare_common("native", self.input, policy, roles(), caps, provider="claude-code", catalog=self.catalog,
                              now=NOW, settings=self.settings, project=lambda *_: {"transport": "none"},
                              **kwargs)["digests"]

        from_file = self.prepare()["digests"]["model_catalog"]
        rebuilt = catalog.Catalog(self.catalog.models, self.catalog.launch)
        self.assertEqual(self.prepare(catalog=rebuilt)["digests"]["model_catalog"], from_file)

    def test_a_changed_engine_changes_the_config_digest(self):
        base = self.prepare()["config"]
        other = self.prepare(settings=dataclasses.replace(self.settings, engine="cao"))["config"]
        self.assertNotEqual(base["digest"], other["digest"])
        self.assertEqual(other["values"]["engine"], "cao")
        again = self.prepare(settings=dataclasses.replace(self.settings, work_source="elsewhere"))["config"]
        self.assertEqual(again["digest"], base["digest"])

class CliCase(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.tmp.cleanup)
        self.root = Path(self.tmp.name)
        home = self.root / "home"
        (home / "skm").mkdir(parents=True)
        patcher = mock.patch.dict(os.environ, {"HOME": str(home), "SKM_HOME": str(home / "skm")})
        patcher.start()
        self.addCleanup(patcher.stop)
        cwd = Path.cwd()
        os.chdir(self.root)
        self.addCleanup(os.chdir, cwd)

    def run_cli(self, *argv: str) -> tuple:
        out, err = io.StringIO(), io.StringIO()
        with redirect_stdout(out), redirect_stderr(err):
            code = main([str(item) for item in argv])
        return code, out.getvalue(), err.getvalue()

    def config(self, text: str) -> Path:
        path = self.root / "invocation.toml"
        path.write_text("schema_version = 1\n" + text, encoding="utf-8")
        return path

    def prepare(self, *extra, provider="claude-code", config=None) -> tuple:
        head = ["--config", config] if config else []
        return self.run_cli(*head, "prepare", "--provider", provider, "--input", INPUT, "--policy", POLICY,
                            "--out", self.root / "out", "--dry-run", "--model-catalog", MODEL_CATALOG, *extra)

    def plan(self, *extra, **kwargs) -> dict:
        code, out, err = self.prepare(*extra, **kwargs)
        self.assertEqual((code, err), (0, ""), out)
        return json.loads(out)

    def binding_decision(self, plan: dict) -> dict:
        return next(item for item in plan["decisions"] if item["kind"] == "binding")

A potential issue involving `skillRef` was identified.

Digest formats are consistent. Launch-plan digests use bare hex. Input digests and skill digests use tagged `sha256:` prefixes. The schema matches.

The `KEY_REUSED` test passes an invalid `submission_id`. It builds the ID from a digest prefix with a `dry-` prefix, but the schema requires a `sub-` prefix. This causes a pattern mismatch and a semantic key collision. The test merely asserts that `KEY_REUSED` appears in the issues.

The test passes because the invalid `submission_id` equals `run_id`, triggering `KEY_REUSED`. Schema validation still runs and fails, but `_errors` collects all issues together, so the error code is `INPUT_INVALID`.

The CLI test also expects refusal. It would pass if KEY_REUSED is printed, but the schema pattern error would also appear. This is not a bug.

The real question is whether a valid submission_id can ever equal run_id. The run_id is built from a digest prefix with a dry- prefix.

A valid submission_id cannot equal run_id because the former requires a `sub-` prefix while the latter uses a `dry-` prefix. The KEY_REUSED check therefore only fires for invalid documents, and the test correctly exercises this impossible case.

I am examining the path pattern more carefully.

The path regex allows `..` but rejects `/`. `capability_ref` uses `_relative`, which can produce paths starting with `..` when the current directory is not an ancestor of the capability file. This creates a mismatch between the regex and the actual paths generated.

Contract 8 forbids home paths in product files. `capability_ref` may embed the home path when `relpath` is computed from a non-ancestor directory.

The home-path concern may be a false alarm. Contract 8 likely applies to documentation and user-facing text, not runtime paths.

I am now scanning the changed product files for plan IDs, PLAN tokens, home paths, and non-English text. The relevant files are CHANGELOG.md, the skiller README, the orchestrator README, and several orchestrator documentation files.

I will also inspect code docstrings and comments for plan IDs or non-English text. I am focusing on the scoped files only, even though git status shows additional uncommitted decision JSON files. I am now looking closely for behavioral bugs.

I found a bug in `is_stale`. The `_moment` helper truncates fractional seconds by splitting on the dot and stripping the Z. This causes `fresh_until < now` to ignore sub-second precision. A record with `fresh_until` at `12:00:00.000Z` and `now` at `12:00:00.500Z` would be incorrectly treated as fresh.

The truncation is intentional. The docstring explicitly states that optional fractions are parsed by stripping them, so timestamps in the same second compare equal. The spec's `< now` comparison is therefore consistent with this design.

The `test_staleness_follows_now` test only exercises whole-second boundaries. It never checks the exact `fresh_until` timestamp or fractional seconds, so the truncation bug is a missed edge case. The contract forbids silently accepting stale records, which makes this discrepancy a real defect.

The reproduction is concrete. A record with `fresh_until` at `12:00:00.100Z` and `now` at `12:00:00.900Z` is silently accepted because `_moment` truncates both to `12:00:00`.     """Resolve the configuration of ``module_id`` from all layers.

    ``schema`` is a :class:`ModuleSchema` or a path to ``config.schema.json``; without it the schema
    is found through ``unit.json`` (``provides.config``) in ``unit_root``. ``project`` is the project
    root (its ``.swissknifeman/config.toml`` is the project layer; ``None`` means no project layer),
    ``config_file`` the ``--config FILE`` layer, ``flags`` a mapping of dotted keys to values from
    the command line (``None`` values are skipped, text values are parsed by the key's type). ``env``
    and ``home`` default to the process environment and home directory. ``warn`` receives the
    ``CONFIG_ENV_UNKNOWN`` notices (default: stderr, once per process and variable); they are also in
    ``ResolvedConfig.warnings``.
    """
    module = _schema_for(module_id, schema, unit_root)
    state = _State(module)
    layers: List[LayerInfo] = [LayerInfo("defaults", None, True)]
    notices: List[str] = []
    environment = os.environ if env is None else env
    warn = warn or _warn_stderr
    prefix: Key = (module_id,)

    machine = Path(machine_config_file(env=environment, home=home))
    candidates: List[Tuple[str, Path]] = [("machine", machine)]
    if project is not None:
        candidates.append(("project", Path(project_config_file(project))))
    for layer, path in candidates:
        info, section, index = _load_file(layer, path, module_id)
        layers.append(info)
        if section:
            state.apply_section(layer, section, file=info.file, index=index, prefix=prefix)
    if project is None:
        layers.insert(2, LayerInfo("project", None, False))

    for extra in extra_layers:
        if extra.name in LAYER_NAMES or not _LAYER_ID.match(extra.name or ""):
            raise ConfigError("CONFIG_FILE_INVALID", f"invalid extra layer name {extra.name!r}")
        if not isinstance(extra.data, Mapping):
            raise ConfigError("CONFIG_TYPE", "extra layer data must be a table", layer=extra.name)
        layers.append(LayerInfo(extra.name, extra.file, bool(extra.data)))
        if extra.data:
            state.apply_section(extra.name, extra.data, file=extra.file, index=extra.index, prefix=(),
